item: assignChaser: a deflected pass leaves the intended receiver as chaser (wrong behaviour, untested)
detail: In /home/user/Fifa/src/ai/steer.ts, ownReceiver() (lines 359-364, used at line 419) claims ball.passTarget as chaser whenever ball.lastKickTeam === team. That claim skips arrival-time selection and hysteresis. passTarget is only cleared by takePossession or a new kick; recordTouch does not clear it, so the claim survives an opponent's deflection. TAI-14's assistedReceiver (src/ai/tactics.ts:515) also requires lastTouchTeam === team and documents that 'a deflection by an opponent ends the assist'; TAI-07 does not. Reproduced twice. (1) Unit probe: pass to slot 9, deflected by opponent 16 (lastTouchTeam = 1), ball near teammate 6. After 60 ticks the chaser is still 9 with ballT 314, while 6 (ballT 24) stays on HOLD_SHAPE. (2) Full step() pipeline: the receiver 40 m away stays chaser for all 90 ticks while a teammate 3.6 m from a stopped ball drifts away. This breaks the brief's 'chosen by arrival time' rule and the glitch line 'two teammates chase or nobody does': nobody near the ball goes for it. The only receiver test (tai-07-chaser.test.ts, 'the intended receiver of our own pass is the chaser') covers an undeflected pass. Fix: also require b.lastTouchTeam === team in ownReceiver, and add a regression test.

item: assignChaser: a fallen intended receiver stays the only chaser, so nobody chases (glitch 'nobody does', untested)
detail: ownReceiver() checks only active === 1. A receiver who goes down while the pass is on its way (FALLEN, actDur 70) is still claimed as team.chaser, and that claim skips the 'chaser who is down is replaced at once' rule (steer.ts line 433). The builder's report says that rule always applies. Reproduced twice. (1) Unit probe: passTarget 9 is FALLEN, teammate 6 is 5 m from the ball (ballT 57 vs 126); chaser = 9, job6 = HOLD_SHAPE. (2) Full step() pipeline: chaser stays 9 for 75+ ticks while he lies on the ground and gets up, and teammate 6 is on SUPPORT and moves away from a slowing ball. The FALLEN-chaser test covers only a non-receiver chaser. Fix: give the receiver claim the same check as other candidates (busyTicks(p) <= chaserHysteresisTicks, or fall through to normal selection), and add a regression test.
